def word_frequency(sentence):

    
    sentence=sentence.split()
    words={}

    
    for i in sentence:
        words[i]=sentence.count(i)
    return words

def word_frequency(sentence):

    sentence=sentence.split()
    words={}

    
    for i in sentence:
        if i in words:
            words[i]+=1
        else:
            words[i]=1

    
    return words


print(word_frequency("python is powerfull python is usefull"))

def student_result(student_marks):
    result={}
    highest=max(student_marks.values())
    average=sum(student_marks.values())/len(student_marks)
    print("highest:",highest)
    print("average:",average)

        if student_marks[i]>=50:
            result[i]="pass"
            print(i," :pass")
        else:
            result[i]="fail"
            print(i,":fail")
    return result

def common_elements(list1, list2):
    result=[]
    for i in list1 :
        if i in list2:
            result.append(i)
    result.sort()
    if len(result)==0:
        return "no common element exist"
    return result

def employee_analysis(employee_data):
    
    salaries=[]
    
    highest_employee=""
    lowest_employee=""
    
    highest_salary=float("-inf")
    lowest_salary=float("inf")
    
    department_count={}
    
    for employee,details in employee_data.items():
        salary=details["salary"]
        department=details["department"]
        salaries.append(salary)
        
        if salary > highest_salary:
            highest_salary=salary
            highest_employee=employee
            
        if salary < lowest_salary:
            lowest_salary=salary
            lowest_employee=employee
            
        if department in department_count:
            department_count[department]+=1
            
        else:
            department_count[department]=1
    average_salary=sum(salaries)/len(salaries)
    above_average=[]
    
    for employee, details in employee_data.items():
        if details["salary"]>average_salary:
            above_average.append(employee)
            
    return {
        "Highest Salary Employee": highest_employee,
        "Lowest Salary Employee": lowest_employee,
        "Average Salary": average_salary,
        "Employees Above Average Salary": above_average,
        "Department-wise Employee Count": department_count
    }   

employee_data = {
    "Rahul": {"salary": 55000, "department": "IT"},
    "Aman": {"salary": 35000, "department": "HR"},
    "Priya": {"salary": 70000, "department": "IT"},
    "Neha": {"salary": 42000, "department": "Finance"},
    "Riya": {"salary": 60000, "department": "IT"}
}

result = employee_analysis(employee_data)
print(result)

def character_statistics(sentence):
    result={
        "vowels":0,
        "consonants":0,
        "digits": 0,
        "space":0,
        "special_character":0
    
    }
    vowels="aeiouAEIOU"
    for i in sentence:
        if i in vowels:
            result["vowels"]+=1
        elif i.isalpha():
            result["consonants"]+=1
        elif i.isdigit():
            result["digits"]+=1
        elif i.isspace():
            result["space"]+=1
        else:
            result["special_character"]+=1
    return result
print(character_statistics("Hello 123 @World"))

Write a function:

def employee_bonus(employee_data):

Input:

{ "Rahul":50000, "Aman":35000, "Priya":70000, "Neha":42000, "Riya":60000 }

Rules:

Salary > 60000 → Bonus 20% Salary > 45000 → Bonus 10% Otherwise → Bonus 5%

In [22]:
def employee_bonus(employee_data):
    bonus={}
    for name, salary in employee_data.items():
        if salary>60000:
            bonus[name]=salary*0.20
        elif salary>45000:
            bonus[name]=salary*0.10
        else:
            bonus[name]=salary*0.05
    return bonus 
print(employee_bonus({ "Rahul":50000, "Aman":35000, "Priya":70000, "Neha":42000, "Riya":60000 }))

def func(students):
    pass_stu={}
    fail_stu={}
    highest={}
    average_marks=[]
    for name, marks in students.items():
        if marks>50:
            pass_stu[name]=marks
        else:
            fail_stu[name]=marks
        highest=max(students,key=students.get)
        average_marks=sum(students.values())/len(students)
    return pass_stu,fail_stu, highest, average_marks

🔴 LEVEL 3 (Company Style) Q5

An online store stores orders like this:

orders = [ {"customer":"Rahul","amount":2500}, {"customer":"Aman","amount":4000}, {"customer":"Rahul","amount":1500}, {"customer":"Priya","amount":5000}, {"customer":"Aman","amount":2000} ]

Find:

Total spending of each customer. Highest spending customer. Average spending of all customers. Customers spending above average.

In [152]:
def func(orders):
    total_spending={}
    for order in orders:
        name=order["customer"]
        amount=order["amount"]
        if name not in total_spending:
            total_spending[name]=0
        total_spending[name]+=amount
    highest_spending=max(total_spending , key=total_spending.get)
    average_value=sum(total_spending.values())/len(total_spending)
    return total_spending,highest_spending, average_value

print(func(orders = [
    {"customer":"Rahul","amount":2500},
    {"customer":"Aman","amount":4000},
    {"customer":"Rahul","amount":1500},
    {"customer":"Priya","amount":5000},
    {"customer":"Aman","amount":2000}
]))

def analyze_numbers(numbers):
   
    maximum=max(numbers)
    minimum=min(numbers)
    average=sum(numbers)/len(numbers)
    count_even=0
    count_odd=0
    for i in numbers:
        if i%2==0:

        else:
            count_odd+=1
    return { "maximum":maximum, "minimum": minimum, "average":average, "total_even":count_even, "total_odd ": count_odd}

Q4

Write a function:

validate_password(password)

Rules:

A valid password must have:

Minimum 8 characters At least one uppercase letter At least one lowercase letter At least one digit At least one special character (@ # $ % & !)

In [39]:
def validate_password(password):
    if len(password)<8:
        return "invalid password"
        
    upper=False
    lower=False
    digit=False
    special=False
    
    special_chars="@#$%&!"
    
    for char in password:
        if char.isupper():
            upper=True
        elif char.islower():
            lower=True
        elif char.isdigit():
            digit=True
        elif char in special_chars:
            special=True 
    if upper and lower and digit and special:
        return "valid password"
    else:
        return"invalid password"

print(validate_password("Hello@123"))      # Valid Password
print(validate_password("hello123"))       # Invalid Password
print(validate_password("HELLO@123"))      # Invalid Password
print(validate_password("Hello123"))       # Invalid Password
print(validate_password("He@1"))           # Invalid Password
print(validate_password("Python@2026"))

def process_marks(marks):
    valid=[]
    for i in marks:
        try:
            valid.append(int(i))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
    avg=sum(valid)/len(valid)
    highest=max(valid)
    return valid, avg, highest

def analyze(data):
    valid_numbers=[]
    invalid_numbers=[]
    for value in data:

        else:
            invalid_numbers.append(value)

        "invalid_numbers": invalid_numbers,
        "sum": sum(valid_numbers),
        "avg":sum(valid_numbers)/len(valid_numbers),
        "maximum":max(valid_numbers)
    }

def analyze_numbers(numbers):
    even_count=0
    odd_count=0
    even_sum=0
    odd_sum=0
    for i in numbers:
        if i%2==0:
            even_count+=1
            even_sum+=i
        else:
            odd_count+=1
            odd_sum+=i
    return{
        "even_count": even_count,
        "odd_count": odd_count,
        "even_sum": even_sum,
        "odd_sum": odd_sum,
        "maximum": max(numbers),
        "minimum": min(numbers)
    }

data = [
    "100",
    "250",
    "abc",
    None,
    "450",
    "-50",
    "300.5",
    "xyz",
    "700"
]
valid_numbers=[]
invalid_numbers=[]
positive=[]
negative=[]
avg=[]
for value in data:
    try:
        if value is None:
            raise ValueError
        num=float(value)
        valid_numbers.append(num)
        if num>0:
            positive.append(num)
        elif num<0:
            negative.append(num)
    except ValueError:
        invalid_numbers.append(num)
avg=sum(valid_numbers)/len(valid_numbers)
print("Valid numbers:", valid_numbers)
print("Invalid values:", invalid_numbers)
print("Positive numbers:", positive)
print("Negative numbers:", negative)
print("Average of valid numbers:", avg)

pivot_table()¶

Definition: pivot_table() summarizes data by grouping rows/columns and applying an aggregation like sum, mean, or count.¶

melt()¶

Definition: melt() converts wide-format data → long-format data.¶

When used: Very useful when data has multiple columns representing categories/time periods and you need to reshape it for EDA, visualization, or analysis.¶

id_vars → column we want to KEEP¶

var_name → new column for old column names¶

value_name → new column for old values¶

In [324]:
sales = pd.DataFrame({
    "Employee": ["Aman", "Riya"],
    "Jan": [50000, 60000],
    "Feb": [55000, 65000],
    "Mar": [60000, 70000]
})
In [332]:
melted=pd.melt(sales, id_vars="Employee", var_name="Months",value_name="Salary")

def func(a):
    series=[]
    dup=[]
    for i in a:
        if i in series:
            if i not in dup:
                dup.append(i)
        else:

    return freq, most_freq

def func(sales):
    total_rev={}
    for items in sales:
        product=items["product"]
        quantity=items["quantity"]
        price=items["price"]
        if product not in total_rev:
            total_rev[product]=quantity*price
        else:
            total_rev[product]+=quantity*price
    highest_product=""
    highest_rev=0
    for product, rev in total_rev.items():
        if rev>highest_rev:
            highest_rev=rev
            highest_product=product
    return  highest_product, highest_rev
